title: Church Discipline
definition: Church discipline is the loving and biblical process by which the Church corrects serious sin, seeks repentance, protects the body, and aims at restoration.
summary: Church discipline seeks repentance, holiness, protection, and restoration within the body of Christ.
christFocus: Jesus gave instruction for correction in the Church, and His goal is truth, holiness, mercy, and restoration rather than revenge.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Church discipline is often misunderstood as harshness, shame, or rejection. Biblically, it is a loving process that takes sin seriously because God is holy and His people matter.

The goal of discipline is not punishment for its own sake. It seeks repentance, restoration, protection of the Church, clarity of witness, and faithfulness to Christ.

Church discipline must be practiced with humility, patience, truth, courage, and grief. Those who restore others must watch themselves and act in a spirit of gentleness.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Unaddressed sin can destroy people and harm the Church. This doctrine matters because love does not ignore what is spiritually dangerous. Biblical correction, rightly practiced, can become a means of mercy and restoration.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Receive correction humbly when Scripture exposes sin. If you must confront another believer, do so gently, biblically, and with a desire for restoration rather than superiority.
